member.name: T:Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.SqlAuthenticationInitializer
member.summary: Initializes authentication providers configured in app.config.
member.remarks: Configured initializers run synchronously during registry bootstrap without holding the lookup/publication lock. Concurrent and reentrant calls observe providers published so far. Only registrations made on the initializer's own thread receive configuration precedence. This uses the current managed thread ID, not logical async context or causal ownership. Work queued to another thread, including Task.Run work that this method waits for, uses application precedence and normal recoverable-error handling (SetProvider returns false). Same-thread calls made before an asynchronous operation yields still receive initializer handling while Initialize is running. Continuations on another thread do not. Initializer status ends when Initialize returns or throws. The registry does not await queued work or async-void continuations, and failures from that work are not automatically captured as initializer failures. GetProvider does not use this thread-ID check. Recoverable initialization or registration failures stop this initializer and are traced, but later configured providers are still attempted. Defaults cannot fill otherwise-unregistered methods after initializer failure because its intended methods are unknown. Explicit application registration can recover a missing method. Fatal failures propagate and are not cached by registry bootstrap. If execution continues, later access can retry bootstrap and repeat initializer side effects. Earlier registrations and initializer side effects are not rolled back. Enable tracing before the first registry access to capture these failures; recoverable initialization failures are not retried until the application restarts.

member.name: M:Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.SqlAuthenticationInitializer.Initialize
member.summary: Registers application-configured authentication providers.
member.remarks: This method executes without the lookup/publication lock. Concurrent and reentrant lookups observe providers published so far and can return null before a method has been initialized. Configuration precedence applies only to registrations made on this thread. Complete required registrations synchronously before returning; asynchronous work does not inherit initializer status through ExecutionContext flow.

Enabled paths report trimming and dynamic-code warnings as applicable. Recoverable registry initialization failures emit diagnostic traces through Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EventSource with the Trace keyword (0x2). Enable tracing before the first registry access to capture configuration-reading, initializer/provider activation and Azure-discovery failures. Recoverable failures in these steps are traced. Activation failures retain their original exceptions. A failed explicit method returns null instead of an earlier provider or Azure default. Failed initializers block defaults for otherwise-unregistered methods. Subsequent lookups of affected methods trace their retained activation failures. Unexpected recoverable bootstrap failures are also cached and logged on later accesses. Unaffected successfully registered providers remain usable. Register an application provider as a workaround, or correct the reported configuration or package version problem and restart the application to retry bootstrap.
User callbacks execute outside the lookup/publication lock. Concurrent or reentrant registration changes cause replacement to recheck precedence and retry callbacks. During bootstrap, concurrent and reentrant lookups see only providers published so far; a method not initialized yet can return null. Outside configured initializer execution, a null provider, unsupported method or recoverable provider callback failure returns false and emits diagnostic traces through Microsoft.Data.SqlClient.EventSource with the Trace keyword (0x2). During a configured initializer, registration errors propagate to the configuration application step and stop that initializer. Recoverable initializer failures are traced, and later configured providers are still attempted. Failed explicit methods cannot use earlier providers or defaults. Failed initializers prevent defaults for unknown intended methods. Application registration can explicitly recover a failed method. Fatal failures propagate, including failures nested in inner or aggregate exceptions. Fatal bootstrap failures are not cached; later access can retry bootstrap and repeat earlier side effects if execution continues. Failed application registrations do not publish the candidate provider. Unexpected recoverable bootstrap failures are cached and traced, but application registration remains available without retrying bootstrap. Existing configuration registrations retain precedence. Correct the reported cause and restart the application to retry failed configuration or discovery.

A failed initializer blocks defaults for otherwise-unregistered methods. Explicit application registration can recover a failed method. Fatal failures propagate. Missing sections and empty optional attributes remain valid.

Enable tracing before the first registry access to capture configuration and discovery failures. Recoverable failed entries are not retried after completed bootstrap. Fatal bootstrap failures are not cached; later access can retry and repeat earlier side effects if execution continues. Activation failures are retained and traced again when affected methods are looked up. Unexpected recoverable bootstrap failures are also cached and traced again. Subsequent calls to can still return successfully registered providers, and can register application providers without retrying bootstrap. Configuration registrations retain precedence. member.summary: The configuration section definition for reading app.config. This infrastructure type is not intended for direct use by application code.

remarks.para: Defines the current SqlClientAuthenticationProviders section for authentication configuration.
This type is public to support use across SqlClient assemblies and configuration section activation. Applications should not instantiate, derive from, or access this type directly.
This sealed handler derives directly from .
Referencing this handler in an app.config section declaration is supported.

This section takes precedence over SqlAuthenticationProviders. An incompatible handler is traced and ignored, allowing the legacy section to be used. Configuration-reading errors produce empty settings without fallback.

Configuration reading uses a relaxed policy that traces and ignores configuration-reading, handler, schema and broker-value errors. Ignoring these errors may select unintended providers or provider settings. Recoverable initializer activation or registration failures stop that initializer, but later configured providers are still attempted. Failed explicit methods retain their activation exceptions and cannot fall back to earlier providers or Azure defaults. Later entries and unrelated defaults remain usable. A failed initializer blocks defaults for otherwise-unregistered methods. Explicit application registration can recover a failed method. Fatal failures propagate. Missing sections and empty optional attributes remain valid.

Enable tracing before the first registry access to capture configuration and discovery failures. Recoverable failed entries are not retried after completed bootstrap. Fatal bootstrap failures are not cached; later access can retry and repeat earlier side effects if execution continues. Activation failures are retained and traced again when affected methods are looked up. Unexpected recoverable bootstrap failures are also cached and traced again. Subsequent calls to can still return successfully registered providers, and can register application providers without retrying bootstrap. Configuration registrations retain precedence. Correct the configuration and restart the application to retry configuration or discovery. Earlier registrations and initializer/provider callback side effects are not rolled back.
